answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a slashable bond before it may vote on work, with one bond buying only one vote. If an agent is caught submitting fabricated reviews, a random audit checks its signed evidence and the contract burns its bond; honest reviewers receive part of the loss. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up capital for each extra identity and risks losing it, rather than gaining influence by minting accounts for free. An ivory haven might sound safe, but even a cedar of cloned agents faces the same per-identity cost.
